messages:
Acme_SRE: Hey team — after the canary rolled out this morning our structured outputs started failing schema validation. We send a strict JSON schema and the responses used to match exactly; now a bunch of fields are coming back as strings or missing. Error rate spiked at ~08:13 UTC. Example: expected typed object, got everything stringified.

Acme_SRE: sample expected vs actual (sanitized):
```json
expected: {
  "user": {
    "id": 12345,
    "email": "ops@acme.com"
  },
  "items": [ { "sku": "ABC", "qty": 2 } ],
  "flags": { "priority": true }
}
actual: {
  "user": "{\"id\":12345,\"email\":\"ops@acme.com\"}",
  "items": "[{\"sku\":\"ABC\",\"qty\":2}]",
  "flags": { "priority": "true" }
}
```

Acme_SRE: Also seeing enum fields return numeric indexes instead of the enum strings (e.g. 0/1 instead of "OPEN"/"CLOSED"). This started right after the canary IDs that deploy-bot posted.

olivia-support: Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the samples. Can you paste one full request_id and the model+version you were routed to when this happened? Any recent changes to request payloads on your side? :pray:

Acme_SRE: request_id 9b3f7a2c (sample) — polling a single route: POST /v1/generate with model "redwood-infer:open-v1.4-quant". No changes on our side. We've pinned schema validation but the client libs are failing on deserialization.

maria.cs: tagging eng-ml and runtime. @ryan-ml can you take a quick look? This sounds like a serialization/formatting regression on a canary.

ryan-ml: thanks @maria.cs — grabbing the deploy timeline. deploy-bot, can you dump the canary rollout events around 1791234000-1791234600? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by ci/cd at 1791233988, step: model-config-update (feature: strict_schema_enforcement=true) -> rolled to 12% at 1791234035 -> 50% at 1791234120 -> 100% at 1791234201.

ryan-ml: ok that flag looks suspicious. strict_schema_enforcement would coerce outputs to the schema but the implementation had a last-minute change to serialization that wraps primitive outputs in strings when enforcement is applied to nested objects. Investigating.

jake.se: assigning to runtime oncall. Quick triage steps for Acme_SRE: can you reproduce with a single curl request? If yes, include the exact curl (headers + body). Also include the full response body and the header X-Model-Version from the response.

Acme_SRE: reproducible. curl below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-infer:open-v1.4-quant","input":"RETURN JSON with fields user.id (int), user.email (string), items (array of objects), flags.priority (boolean)","format":"json"}'
```

Acme_SRE: Response body (abbreviated):
```json
{
  "output": "{\"user\":\"{\\\"id\\\":12345,\\\"email\\\":\\\"ops@acme.com\\\"}\", \"items\":\"[{\\\"sku\\\":\\\"ABC\\\",\\\"qty\\\":2}]\", \"flags\":{\"priority\":\"true\"}}"
}
```

olivia-support: got it. We'll escalate and request a rollback if needed, but first engineering needs the model version header and any route logs for that request_id.

jake.se: standing by. @ryan-ml, initial hunch: the serialization layer added an escape+stringify path when strict_schema_enforcement is true and the output generator returns a pre-serialized JSON. That double-serializes into strings. If so, rapid mitigation is to flip the flag off for the affected model pool.

ryan-ml: confirming in canary logs: found transformation step "schema_enforcer.v2" applying json.dumps on nested objects. There was a patch intended to handle nulls but it didn't check type before dumping. Example log: 
```
[1791234105] transform: schema_enforcer.v2 applied to output -> detected nested dict -> json.dumps -> wrote string
```
ryan-ml: I'm going to open a rollback PR to disable strict_schema_enforcement on redwood-infer:open-v1.4-quant and revert the schema_enforcer.v2 change. ETA ~12-18m.

maria.cs: can you confirm impact surface? Which customers hit this? Acme_SRE reported but we should query error rates. Use quick query: 
```bash
# counts of schema-validation errors by customer in last 1h
grep -R "schema-validation-failed" /var/log/infra | grep 1791234 | sort | uniq -c
```

jake.se: ran the query in staging logs, results show about 18 distinct customer IDs with increased schema failures, most hitting quantized pools in us-west.

olivia-support: heads-up to CS: I'm drafting a customer message explaining we identified a regression tied to a canary flag, mitigation is in progress and a temporary workaround is to set format=json-raw (server will skip schema_enforcer). Will follow up with ETA. :writing_hand:

Acme_SRE: Appreciate the rapid response. For our app the workaround is fine short-term. Please tell me when you've rolled back and we'll re-run our validation.

ryan-ml: rollback PR merged and deployed to canary at 1791234410, removed strict_schema_enforcement for redwood-infer:open-v1.4-quant. Full rollback to 100% at 1791234550.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed: model-config-update reverted for redwood-infer:open-v1.4-quant.

jake.se: Can we confirm with Acme_SRE that the same curl now returns properly typed JSON (no wrapped strings)?

Acme_SRE: re-tested at 1791234600 — response looks correct now. Example:
```json
{
  "user": { "id": 12345, "email": "ops@acme.com" },
  "items": [ { "sku": "ABC", "qty": 2 } ],
  "flags": { "priority": true }
}
```

olivia-support: closing loop with customer and filing a postmortem. Action items: (1) add type-check before json.dumps in schema_enforcer, (2) add unit test for pre-serialized outputs, (3) add alert when schema_enforcer.toggle changes on a model pool, (4) CS notify customers in window.

maria.cs: thanks everyone. tagging this for the postmortem doc. Acme_SRE — we'll follow up with a timeline and root cause write-up. :white_check_mark:
